liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Will Take You Home** (3 reviews): Reviewer disliked I Will Take You Home in set two, their least favorite song then; Reviewer, a big Brent fan, always liked this Take You Home [18][24][27]
- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Shakedown Street opener described as chunky; Shakedown Street includes a nicely extended, jazzy jam [19][28]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Estimated Prophet opened set two, leading into Scarlet Begonias and Crazy Fingers, which the reviewer called unusual; Estimated Prophet opening the second set is rare, going into Scarlet, Crazy Fingers and Playin' [19][24]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Sugaree was well played but uninspiring, with a strangely lethargic ending [28]
- **The Promised Land** (1 review): Promised Land as first-set closer was the reviewer's long-time favorite choice for that slot [24]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet Begonias counted among the best the reviewer had heard, with Jerry ripping through it [20]
- **Space** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Space the best ever, crediting Mickey Hart and finding it extremely trippy [27]
- **And We Bid You Goodnight** (1 review): The Bid You Goodnight encore was singled out as a treat [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-04-03.mtx.hansokolow.97566.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 167 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1990-04-03.158650.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 166 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1990-04-03.158672.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: soundboard; 20 songs; 166 min [3]
- **gd90-04-03.nak.gardner.3577.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 10 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording with fair to good sound quality [28]
- **gd90-04-03.sbd.hinko.17811.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 164 min; rated 4.04/5 by 26 [14]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears muffled sound with Weir's guitar barely audible [26]

## Around the show

- Reviewer found the second-set song order unusual, which they felt improved the show [18]
- Reviewer's favorite of the three-night run [19]
- Reviewer thought Albany a week earlier would be hard to beat, but this show comes close [20]
- Reviewer places this show in the top five of 1990 [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-04-03.mtx.hansokolow.97566.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: matrix of SBD: shnid=17811 and AUD: shnid=3732 by hansokolow using ProTools [1]. Also: Matrix made by hansokolow in ProTools, combining a soundboard source with an audience source; Soundboard chain: master cassette to Sonic Solutions at 24 bits, to CD, then EAC and SHN; Audience source: front-of-board Nak 300/CP4 and Sennheiser 441 pairs, through a Sony mixer to Sony D10 Pro [1]
- **gd1990-04-03.158650.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 14, 2022; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several masters were combined to complete the show [2]
- **gd1990-04-03.158672.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 14, 2022; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X) [3]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy, with multiple masters used to complete the show; This is a downsampled copy of the 24-bit/96k release 158650, converted to 16-bit/44.1k [3]
- **gd90-04-03.nak.gardner.3577.sbeok.shnf**: source: Nak 300/CP4's > PMD 420 by Alan Wallace, tapers section [5]
- **gd90-04-03.sbd.hinko.17811.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard Master Cassette > Sonic Solutions @ 24 bits > CD (Sony Super Bit Mapping 2) > EAC > SHN (seekable) [14]

## Art and photos

- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 4/3/90 The Omni, Atlanta, GA | Sprin…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27109709510/) [30]
